claim: The survey of LLM-based agents for software engineering collects 124 papers and categorizes them from the software engineering and agent perspectives.
quote: We collect 124 papers and categorize them from two perspectives, i.e., the SE and agent perspectives.

claim: OpenHands is described by its authors as a platform for agents that interact with the world in similar ways to those of a human developer.
quote: we introduce OpenHands (f.k.a. OpenDevin), a platform for the development of powerful and flexible AI agents that interact with the world in similar ways to those of a human developer: by writing code, interacting with a command line, and browsing the web.

claim: The OpenHands related-work section says that AutoCodeRover addresses GitHub issues via code search and abstract syntax tree manipulation.
quote: AutoCodeRover Zhang et al. (2024b) addresses GitHub issues via code search and abstract syntax tree manipulation.

claim: The AutoCodeRover authors state that software engineering involves program improvement apart from coding, specifically software maintenance and software evolution.
quote: Nevertheless, software engineering involves the process of program improvement apart from coding, specifically to enable software maintenance (e.g. bug fixing) and software evolution (e.g. feature additions).

claim: The agent survey describes SWE-bench as the first benchmark for end-to-end software maintenance, with 2,294 real-world GitHub issues across 12 popular Python repositories.
quote: SWE-bench [252] is the first benchmark for end-to-end software maintenance, which consists of 2,294 real-world GitHub issues across 12 popular Python repositories.

claim: The AutoCodeRover authors argue that the toughest challenge in program repair lies in inferring the intent of the developer or the specification.
quote: From the point of view of program repair, the toughest challenge lies in inferring the intent of the developer or the specification.

claim: The DRMiner authors report that developers may lack motivation to document design rationales when they will not gain immediate benefit.
quote: However, there may be a lack of motivation for developers to document design rationales (i.e., the design alternatives and the underlying arguments for making or rejecting decisions) when they will not gain immediate benefit, resulting in a lack of standard capture of these rationales.

claim: The same authors report that advanced LLMs prompted with the mined rationales generate 10×-18× more full-match patches in automated program repair.
quote: Furthermore, we investigate the usefulness of the design rationales mined by DRMiner for automated program repair (APR) and find that advanced LLMs, when prompted with these extracted rationales, generate 10×-18× more full-match patches and achieve a 10%-13% gain in CodeBLEU scores.

claim: The requirements traceability study states that understanding the relation between artifacts is crucial for understanding the system and for supporting tasks such as change impact analysis.
quote: Understanding the relation between these artifacts is crucial for understanding the system and for supporting tasks such as change impact analysis and software reusability [1], [2].

claim: The chapter on NLP for traceability notes that it is not yet clear how LLM-based approaches to trace link creation will scale.
quote: As hinted by the latest work on Generative AI, the conversational interface backed by large language models serves as an intuitive way for trace link creation and explanation, but it is not yet clear how these approaches will scale.

claim: The authors of the comparative study of OpenHands, SWE-agent and Prometheus state that current evaluations treat agents as black boxes, focusing primarily on success rates while overlooking the rich information contained in their execution trajectories.
quote: current evaluations treat agents as black boxes, focusing primarily on success rates while overlooking the rich information contained in their execution trajectories

claim: The empirical study of OpenHands, SWE-agent and Prometheus trajectories reports that failed trajectories are consistently longer and exhibit higher variance than successful ones, with failure patterns differing significantly between agents.
quote: we find that failed trajectories are consistently longer and exhibit higher variance than successful ones, with failure patterns differing significantly between agents.

claim: On localization, the SWE-bench trajectory study finds that most trajectories identify the problematic files correctly, even in failures.
quote: Third, our fault localisation analysis shows that while most trajectories correctly identify problematic files (72-81\% even in failures), success depends more on achieving approximate rather than exact code modifications.

claim: SWE-agent's own appendix describes an automated categorization of 248 unresolved trajectories, validated against only 15 hand-labelled instances.
quote: A validation set of 15 instances are then sampled from the 248 instances left marked unresolved by SWE-agent and the authors hand-label them according to these categories.

claim: DeFA, a dependency-guided attribution framework, is described as identifying the decisive error, responsible agent, and error category.
quote: Finally, DeFA uses step evidence and the steps' roles in failure propagation to identify the decisive error, responsible agent, and error category.

claim: A zero-replay debugging study reports that step-level attribution by an LLM judge reached only 0.14-0.52 accuracy on Who&When.
quote: Who&When judge [5] LLM-as-judge (no replay) agent / step step acc. (Who&When) 0.14-0.52

claim: The same work states that counterfactual replay is reliable but its cost grows linearly with candidate events.
quote: Replay is reliable but its cost grows linearly with candidate events:

claim: DRMiner's authors report that developers may lack motivation to document design rationales when they gain no immediate benefit, which leaves rationales without a standard capture.
quote: However, there may be a lack of motivation for developers to document design rationales (i.e., the design alternatives and the underlying arguments for making or rejecting decisions) when they will not gain immediate benefit, resulting in a lack of standard capture of these rationales.

claim: DRMiner is an approach that mines latent design rationales from developers' live discussion in open-source issue logs in Jira.
quote: automatically mine latent design rationales from developers’ live discussion in open-source community (i.e., issue logs in Jira)

claim: In the DRMiner evaluation, advanced LLMs prompted with the extracted rationales generated 10×-18× more full-match patches in automated program repair and gained 10%-13% in CodeBLEU.
quote: find that advanced LLMs, when prompted with these extracted rationales, generate 10×-18× more full-match patches and achieve a 10%-13% gain in CodeBLEU scores.

claim: gIBIS is an application-specific hypertext system designed to facilitate the capture of early design deliberations.
quote: This paper describes an application-specific hypertext system designed to facilitate the capture of early design deliberations.

claim: The authors of the gIBIS paper reported that early experiments suggested the IBIS method was still incomplete.
quote: Early experiments suggest that the IBIS method is still incomplete

claim: The LLMoxie report states that coding agents leave decision trails that are difficult to reconstruct after the fact.
quote: Off-the-shelf coding agents produce running Python while ignoring the conventions of the communities whose libraries they invoke [3,17], mishandle sensitive or embargoed data [11], and leave decision trails that are difficult to reconstruct after the fact [30].

claim: LLMoxie's authors describe current agentic practice as lacking mechanisms analogous to version control for tracking the provenance of AI-assisted contributions, which accumulates what they call intent debt.
quote: However, current agentic AI practices lack mechanisms analogous to version control or commit history for tracking the provenance of AI-assisted contributions, accumulating what has been termed intent debt: the absence of externalized rationale that developers and AI agents alike need in order to safely evolve a system [30].
locator: sec. Production Deployment on Azure, para 36

claim: The LLMoxie report's operational lessons rest on practitioner observation and project artifacts rather than a controlled user study.
quote: the operational lessons in Section 6 are based on practitioner observation and project artifacts rather than a controlled user study

claim: The Natural Language Processing for Requirements Traceability chapter states that TLR approaches often lack large enough and credible datasets.
quote: TLR approaches often lack large enough and credible datasets.
locator: sec. Limitations and Concluding Remarks, para 47

claim: The same chapter reports that none of the automated trace recovery approaches are sufficiently good to be useful when dealing with real-world, safety-critical systems.
quote: In practice, none of the automated trace recovery approaches are sufficiently good to be useful when dealing with real-world, safety-critical systems [27].

claim: In the security-requirements study that linked requirements to goal models with GPT-3.5-turbo, the approach and tool yielded positive results, demonstrating a precision of 100%, a recall of 78.5%, and an F1-score of 87.9%.
quote: The approach and tool yielded positive results, demonstrating a precision of 100%, a recall of 78.5%, and an F1-score of 87.9%.

claim: The bidirectional-convergence study reported that combining forward and backward recovery of use cases raised use-case recovery coverage from 65.5% to 75.1%.
quote: This bidirectional convergence approach increased use-case recovery coverage from 65.5% to 75.1%, a gain of 9.6 percentage points, and improved trace-link recall.

claim: The inter-requirements ensemble study found that small LLMs reduce the candidate space with minimal loss of recall.
quote: Furthermore, small LLMs effectively reduce the candidate space with minimal loss of recall.

claim: In the study of LLM ensembles for candidate filtering in inter-requirements traceability, the authors report that while their LLM-based ensemble approach achieves comparable F2-scores to IR methods, it lags in precision.
quote: While our LLM-based ensemble approach achieves comparable F2-scores to IR methods, it lags in precision.

claim: LightTraceLLM reported traceability performance comparable to a high-end baseline while cutting monetary inference cost by approximately 67-99%.
quote: An extensive empirical evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets shows that the proposed approaches achieve traceability performance comparable to the high-end baseline while reducing monetary inference cost by approximately $\mathbf{6 7 - 9 9 \%}$, depending on the method and dataset.

claim: TraceLLM concluded that traceability performance depends critically on the quality of prompt engineering.
quote: Overall, our findings highlight that traceability performance depends not only on model capacity but also critically on the quality of prompt engineering.

claim: The NL-PL study reports that relying solely on textual similarity is limited by the semantic gap between natural-language and programming-language artifacts.
quote: However, in tasks involving natural language and programming language (NL-PL) artifacts, relying solely on textual similarity is limited by their semantic gap.

claim: The AutoCodeRover authors state that the toughest challenge in program repair lies in inferring the developer's intent or specification.
quote: From the point of view of program repair, the toughest challenge lies in inferring the intent of the developer or the specification.

claim: AutoCodeRover gleans that intent from the project structure.
quote: The outlook of AutoCodeRover is that the developer intent is gleaned from the project structure for automated program modifications.

claim: The SpecRover authors describe their approach as more general, inferring specifications from program structure, program behavior, tests and other sources.
quote: In contrast, SpecRover is more general and is capable of inferring specifications from different sources including program structure, program behavior, tests and so on.

claim: The SpecRover authors state that the reviewer agent can produce evidence of correctness for automatically generated fixes, such as an explanation of the patch, a reproducer test, and the accumulated specifications from different code elements.
quote: The reviewer agent can produce evidence of correctness of automatically generated fixes -such as explanation of patch, reproducer test, and the accumulated specifications from different code elements.

claim: On SWE-bench Lite, SpecRover reports resolving 31% of issues.
quote: Our tool shows high efficacy, solving 19.3% issues in full SWE-bench and 31% on SWE-bench lite.

claim: In SpecRover's analysis of 207 unresolved SWE-bench Lite tasks, 107 (51.7%) had ambiguous issue descriptions, 61 (29.5%) had an incorrect fix location, and 39 (18.8%) had incorrect code modifications.
quote: 1) Ambiguous issue description (as labeled by SWE-bench Verified [22]): 107 (51.7%) 2) Incorrect fix location: 61 (29.5%) 3) Incorrect code modification: 39 (18.8%)

claim: The AutoCodeRover authors acknowledge that a patch passing the added tests may still be overfitting.
quote: However, this patch may be overfitting.

claim: The test-driven survey concludes that passing tests alone does not establish behavioral equivalence, effective feedback, or process adherence.
quote: Test passing alone does not establish behavioral equivalence, effective feedback, or process adherence; aggregate improvements can also conceal different outcomes across models, tasks, and denominators.

claim: The OSS-Fuzz study similarly finds that patches with high CodeBLEU scores still fail the given exploit input.
quote: since patches with high CodeBLEU scores still fail to pass given the given exploit input

claim: The authors of History Driven Program Repair state their main insight as follows: recurring bug fixes are common in real-world applications, and previously-appearing fix patterns can provide useful guidance to an automated repair technique.
quote: Our main insight is that recurring bug fixes are common inreal-world applications, and that previously-appearing fix patterns canprovide useful guidance to an automated repair technique.

claim: Getafix, which learns fix patterns from past human-written fixes for static-analysis bug categories, is reported to predict exactly the human-written fix as the top-most suggestion between 12% and 91% of the time, depending on the bug category.
quote: The approach predicts exactly the human-written fix as the top-most suggestion between 12% and 91% of the time, depending on the bug category.

claim: FixMiner addresses how patterns are mined, and its authors argue that earlier approaches often do not yield fix patterns that are tractable and reusable as actionable input to APR systems.
quote: While the literature includes various approaches leveraging similarity among patches to guide program repair, these approaches often do not yield fix patterns that are tractable and reusable as actionable input to APR systems.

claim: The FixMiner authors report that their mined patterns let the PARFixMiner prototype correctly fix 26 Defects4J bugs.
quote: We further integrated the mined patterns to an automated program repair prototype, PARFixMiner, with which we are able to correctly fix 26 bugs of the Defects4J benchmark.

claim: RepairAgent is described as treating the LLM as an agent that autonomously plans and executes actions to fix bugs by invoking suitable tools.
quote: Unlike existing deep learning-based approaches, which prompt a model with a fixed prompt or in a fixed feedback loop, our work treats the LLM as an agent capable of autonomously planning and executing actions to fix bugs by invoking suitable tools.

claim: DRMiner reports that advanced LLMs, when prompted with mined design rationales, generate 10×-18× more full-match patches.
quote: Furthermore, we investigate the usefulness of the design rationales mined by DRMiner for automated program repair (APR) and find that advanced LLMs, when prompted with these extracted rationales, generate 10×-18× more full-match patches and achieve a 10%-13% gain in CodeBLEU scores.

claim: The SWE-bench-Live authors state that SWE-bench and its variants have become standard for evaluating LLMs on the issue resolution task.
quote: Among them, SWE-bench [10] and its variants, such as Multimodal SWE-bench [22] and Multi-SWE-bench [25], have become standard for evaluating LLMs on the issue resolution task

claim: The SWE-bench-Live authors report that the same agent-LLM pair consistently performs worse on SWE-bench-Live than on SWE-bench.
quote: To explore this discrepancy further, we conduct a controlled comparison and find that the same agent-LLM pair consistently performs worse on SWE-bench-Live than on SWE-bench.

claim: The same authors suggest that existing models may be overfitting to static benchmarks.
quote: This finding suggests that existing models may be overfitting to static benchmarks like SWE-bench, underscoring the importance of developing more dynamic and diverse evaluation settings, such as those provided by SWE-bench-Live.

claim: The SWE-bench-java authors note that SWE-bench is centered on Python and does not cover fields such as web applications, mobile applications, and system programming.
quote: However, it does not cover other common and necessary fields like web applications, mobile applications, and system programming, which rely on other programming languages [7,8].

claim: The large-scale trajectory study finds that the widely reported correlation between trajectory length and failure reverses direction once task difficulty is controlled.
quote: The widely reported correlation between trajectory length and failure reverses direction once task difficulty is controlled, revealing it as a confound.

claim: The debugging study of multi-agent traces cautions that its calibration may not transfer perfectly to production agent systems.
quote: Calibration may not transfer perfectly to production agent systems.
locator: sec. Limitations and Threats to Validity, para 58
